summary: Reviewed 2 implementation files (knowledge.ts, knowledge-store.ts) plus schema/knowledge.ts, storage/atomic-writer.ts, utils/ledger-root.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 3 Low/Info observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Info — A05 Security Misconfiguration: Error messages returned to MCP clients include (error as Error).message, which can expose full filesystem paths (e.g., 'Failed to write JSON to /Users/…/global-insights.json'). For a local dev tool this is acceptable, but wrapping storage-layer errors at the tool boundary (stripping path details) would be a defence-in-depth improvement. See knowledge.ts addInsight/searchInsights/listInsights/updateInsight catch blocks.

Info — A04 Insecure Design: InsightSchema fields title, content, category, source, and tags[] have no max-length or max-cardinality constraints in schema/knowledge.ts. For a local filesystem tool this poses no meaningful DoS risk, but adding length bounds (e.g., z.string().max(10000)) would make the schema self-documenting and guard against accidental bulk writes.

Info — A04 Insecure Design: The confidence field (InsightSchema) accepts any number with no range validation — values outside 0–1 are silently accepted. No security impact, but a z.number().min(0).max(1) constraint would enforce the documented semantic.

Info — A01 Broken Access Control (design note, not a vulnerability): updateInsight in knowledge-store.ts scans store files alphabetically via _enumerateStorePaths(), so global-insights.json is searched before {slug}-insights.json files. An agent supplying a numeric ID that collides with a global insight when intending to update a project-scoped insight will update the global one. No privilege escalation is possible (single-user local tool), but the behaviour is subtle. Adding an optional scope/project_slug filter parameter to ledger_update_insight would make the intent unambiguous. Previously flagged by QA — recorded here for the code reviewer.

summary: Code review PASS. No blocking issues found. Architecture is clean, patterns are consistent with the rest of the codebase, and the implementation satisfies all 9 acceptance criteria.

Storage layer (knowledge-store.ts): well-structured with correct atomic-write + file-lock pattern throughout. All read-modify-write sequences (addInsight, updateInsight) run under a single withLock call. Pure reads intentionally bypass the lock, consistent with LedgerStore precedent. Deadlock avoidance correctly handled by bypassing writeGlobalStore/writeProjectStore from inside CRUD methods.

Schema layer (schema/knowledge.ts): PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX is the single source of truth shared between InsightSchema.project_slug and KnowledgeStoreManager._validateSlug — defence-in-depth path traversal protection is solid.

Tool layer (knowledge.ts): clean delegation to KnowledgeStoreManager. Zod schemas follow the no-.refine() constraint. _internal export follows §53 convention. Tool registration and help content are complete.
One DRY observation recorded: formatInsightId() in knowledge.ts duplicates the KN-NNNN format from nextId() in knowledge-store.ts. Not blocking — documented as an improvement comment.

Two documentation gaps tagged as documentation-forward for the Documentation agent: (1) per-store ID scoping not documented in api-surface.md; (2) updateInsight alphabetical scan order not captured at the API surface level.

comments.note: DRY violation: formatInsightId() in knowledge.ts and nextId() in knowledge-store.ts both produce identical `KN-${id.padStart(4, '0')}` output. Since nextId() is a public API with dedicated tests, the cleanest fix is to export a pure formatInsightId() utility from schema/knowledge.ts (zero-dependency layer) so both consumers share one definition. Not blocking — no behavioral impact — but creates a divergence risk if the KN-NNNN format ever changes.

nextId() design note: the method is public, mutates the store in-place, and returns a formatted KN-NNNN string — but the return value is always discarded by addInsight() (which needs the numeric id instead). The method name does not communicate the mutation side-effect clearly. A future rename to incrementNextId() (void) + separate formatInsightId() (pure) would remove the ambiguity. Not blocking; behaviour is correct and the comment in addInsight() explains the intent.

[documentation-forward] InsightSchema.id is per-store (not globally unique across stores). The formatted_id (KN-NNNN) returned by all 4 tools is also only unique within its store. This constraint is documented in knowledge.test.ts but not in api-surface.md or the tool descriptions. Update api-surface.md: (1) InsightSchema entry should note 'id is per-store; not unique across global and project stores'; (2) ledger_add_insight and ledger_update_insight tool entries should note 'formatted_id is store-scoped'.

[documentation-forward] updateInsight() in knowledge-store.ts scans stores via _enumerateStorePaths() which returns files in filesystem order (alphabetical on most platforms), so global-insights.json is always searched before {slug}-insights.json. If a global insight and a project insight share the same numeric id, the global one is updated. This behaviour is documented in knowledge.test.ts (line 393–394) and flagged by QA and Security Auditor, but is absent from api-surface.md. Add a note to KnowledgeStoreManager.updateInsight() in api-surface.md: 'Stores are scanned in alphabetical order; global-insights.json precedes project-scoped stores. Pass an id that is unique across stores, or use a future scope/project_slug filter when available.'

[documentation-forward] writeGlobalStore() and writeProjectStore() carry a @warning comment in source (do not call from inside a withLock callback — risk of deadlock), but this invariant is not captured in api-surface.md. Add the deadlock warning to the api-surface.md entries for both methods so future developers consulting the manifest are alerted without needing to read the source.
